data.rationale: The fuzz target secilc-fuzzer parses attacker-controlled CIL text (cil_add_file/cil_compile/cil_build_policydb), so any post-parse pass is reachable. The deny-rule feature (new in 3.6-rc1, cil_deny.c) rewrites (deny ...) rules into allow rules by synthesizing typeattributes. In cil_create_attribute_* helpers an ebitmap of type values is computed with max = db->num_types and, when the bitmap has exactly one bit, code does 'unsigned i = ebitmap_highest_set_bit(types); *d3 = DATUM(db->val_to_type[i]);' (lines 941-944, and similarly 1001-1007 and 1061-1067). db->val_to_type is allocated in __cil_post_db_array_helper (cil_post.c:696) with exactly db->num_types entries and indexed by type->value. There is no bounds check on i against num_types here, and the deny pass runs before/independently of the value-assignment bookkeeping, so an index >= num_types (or val_to_type still NULL for a policy whose only types come from deny-synthesized attributes) yields an out-of-bounds read. Similar unchecked patterns: cil_datums_andnot (cil_deny.c:717) dereferences a1->types->highbit without a NULL/empty guard. Random fuzzing with CIL seeds did not reproduce in ~5 minutes, so reachability needs a crafted deny/attribute combination; this location is the best-supported root cause candidate from code review.
